name: Omri
bio:
Omri was the commander of Israel's army, encamped against the Philistine town of Gibbethon, when news reached the troops that Zimri had assassinated King Elah and seized the throne. The army made Omri king on the spot; he marched to Tirzah and besieged it, and when Zimri saw the city was falling, he burned the royal palace down around himself rather than be captured (1 Kings 16:15-18). Israel then split into two factions, half following Tibni son of Ginath and half following Omri; Omri's faction prevailed, Tibni died, and Omri became sole king (1 Kings 16:21-22).

Omri bought the hill of Samaria from a man named Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, naming it Samaria after him — the city that would remain the capital of the northern kingdom for the rest of its history. Yet Scripture records that Omri did more evil in the LORD's eyes than any king before him, walking in the ways of Jeroboam and leading Israel further into sin (1 Kings 16:23-26). Omri reigned twelve years in all; when he died, he was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab succeeded him (1 Kings 16:27-28).
